summary.oneLiner: SK Minerals pivoted from pure trading to high-margin manufacturing (23% of rev), driven by a unique first-in-India halogen-free flame retardant plant currently in trials. The core investment thesis rests on scaling this proprietary capacity from 600 MT to 18,000 MT over 18 months, targeting 40% EBITDA margins vs. 21% trading margins, backed by a Rs. 55 Cr order book (76% government).

one-line thesis: SK Minerals pivoted from pure trading to high-margin manufacturing (23% of rev), driven by a unique first-in-India halogen-free flame retardant plant currently in trials. The core investment thesis rests on scaling this proprietary capacity from 600 MT to 18,000 MT over 18 months, targeting 40% EBITDA margins vs. 21% trading margins, backed by a Rs. 55 Cr order book (76% government).
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs. 318 Cr (+50% YoY); EBITDA Margin: 10% (up from 9%); PAT Margin: 6% (up from 5%); Order Book: Rs. 55 Cr (Rs. 42 Cr Govt, Rs. 13 Cr Private); Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, but working capital cycle is 110 days. One-offs/Distortions: H2 FY26 revenue surge driven by raw material price inflation (Jan-Mar) and strategic stockpiling pre-price hike, masking pure volume growth; margin contraction in H2 due to input cost lag.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Targeting sustained momentum (historical 3x CAGR); Margin: Manufacturing ~30%, New Polymer Additives ~40%, Trading ~21%; Order Inflow: Strong pipeline in cable/wire sector; Capex/Commissioning: Rs. 20 Cr planned for FY27-FY28 to scale polymer capacity to 18,000 MT in 12-18 months.
order book & pipeline: Rs. 55 Crores total; Composition: 76% Government (1-year contracts), 24% Private (3-month/quantity contracts); Execution cycle varies by customer type.
segment / subsidiary detail: Feed & Food Additives: 95% capacity utilization, 30% gross margin; Trading (Base Oils, TG Urea): 21% gross margin; Polymer Additives (New): 400 MT/month plant in trial phase (teething issues), targeting 40% margin, expected full operation in 3-6 months.
growth verticals / optionality: Scale polymer additive capacity from current 600 MT/year to 18,000 MT/year over next 18 months on 9.6-acre acquired land; Future entry into EV battery additives segment; R&D pipeline includes Omega-3 and Vitamin D2 (pilot stage).
margins & cost dynamics: Current blended EBITDA 10%; Manufacturing gross margin 30%; Trading gross margin 21%; New polymer products targeted at 40% gross margin. Cost pressure from imported raw materials (100% advance payment terms for some giants) impacting H2 margins.
capex / expansion: Rs. 20 Crores planned for FY27-FY28 specifically for polymer additive expansion and compounding facility; Funding mix: IPO proceeds + Bank credit lines.
capital allocation: Focus on capacity expansion (polymer segment) and working capital management (reducing 110-day cycle via invoice discounting); No dividend guidance provided.
risks & watch-items: Raw material import dependency (geopolitical supply chain); Working capital strain (110 days); Teething problems in new polymer plant delaying commercialization; Customer concentration in government contracts; Replication risk despite claimed R&D barriers.
management quality / tone: Confident on technology moat ('Blue Ocean', 'First in India'), cautious on timelines (3-6 months for trials), aggressive on capacity scaling (18,000 MT target).
non-obvious takeaways: The company is not just a trader but a niche chemistries player leveraging nitrogen-phosphorus chemistry; The 400 MT/month polymer plant is currently underutilized due to 'mechanical composition' testing at customer ends, not just production issues; Management claims no direct domestic competition for halogen-free variants, relying on technical/R&D barriers rather than patents (3 patents to be filed soon).
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fire safety regulations tightening in India due to recent incidents; need for non-toxic smoke emission materials. | SK Minerals & Additives Ltd | beneficiary | High | Only domestic manufacturer of halogen-free flame retardants; addressing a critical gap in cable/wire and electrical sectors with 40% margin potential vs. 21% trading. |

themes.title: Industrial gases, chlor-alkali & commodity chemicals
themes.need: A capacity-led commodity-chemical and industrial-gas cycle underpins the basic-materials chain - ELLEN on air-separation/industrial gases; EPIGRAL/CHEMPLASTS/DCW/DCMSHRIRAM/GHCL/TATACHEM/GNFC on chlor-alkali, soda-ash and vinyls; LORDSCHLO on caustic; CHEMBONDCH on water-treatment chemicals. Pricing/utilization and energy costs are the near-term swing factors.
themes.driver: Caustic/soda-ash price recovery; utilization ramp on new capacity; energy-cost relief.
